title: [For kids] How do I mark my chore as done?
content:
Tap the chore on your dashboard and hit Done. If your parent asked for a photo, take one first - that's your proof it's finished.

Some chores pay you straight away. Others go to your parent to check first - you'll see it sitting under Waiting until they look at it.

title: [For kids] Why is my chore waiting to be checked?
content: Some chores need your parent to check them before you get paid - that's normal, not a sign anything's wrong. Once they approve it, the money is added straight away.

title: [For kids] My parent sent my chore back - what now?
content: If a chore comes back to you, your parent wants something fixed or finished before they can pay you for it. There's usually a note explaining what to change. Fix it and send it again - you can go back and forth as many times as you need, and you won't lose anything by trying again.

title: [For kids] How do I set up a savings goal?
content: Tap New Goal, give it a name, pick a category, set how much you need, and choose a date you'd like to reach it by. You can have up to 5 goals going at once, so you can save for more than one thing.

title: [For kids] Can my parent help me save up faster?
content: Yes - some parents add extra money toward a goal to help you get there sooner, either as an ongoing top-up or a one-off gift. If that happens, you'll see your saved amount jump - it's real money added to your goal, not just for show.

title: [For kids] Why did the app ask me to wait before I spent money?
content: If you're about to spend a big chunk of what you have, Morechard shows you a quick "just checking" screen before you go ahead. It's not stopping you - you can still choose I'm sure, log it - it's just a moment to think it over first in case you'd rather wait.

title: [For kids] I forgot my code - what do I do?
content: You can't reset it yourself - ask a parent to reset your code for you from their dashboard. Once they've done that, you'll be able to get back in with the new code.

title: [For kids] Can my parents see everything I do in the app?
content: Your parents can see what you've earned, saved, and spent - that's how they approve chores and help with goals. What they can't see is anything private like your exact location - proof photos are only used to check a chore was actually done, not to track where you are.

title: [For kids] What are the Learning Lab lessons, and why do I get them?
content:
Learning Lab is a set of short lessons about money - things like saving, spending wisely, and how interest works. You don't do them in order; a new one unlocks when something you've actually done (like reaching a savings goal, or going a while without spending) makes that lesson useful right then. Each one only takes about 15 - 25 minutes: a quick intro, a short lesson, something to try, and a quiz at the end.

Not every family has Learning Lab turned on - if you don't see it, that's just how your account is set up, not something broken.

title: [For kids] Can I chat with the AI?
content: Not right now. The Mentor sends you helpful messages based on what's happening with your money, but you can't type back and forth with it like a chat. If that ever changes, it'll be something new you'd be told about - not something that quietly turns on.

title: [For kids] How do I give money to a good cause?
content: If you've got a Give jar, you can send a request from there to give some of your money to a cause you care about. Your parent gets notified and needs to approve it before it goes through.

title: [For kids] Why can't things in my history just be deleted?
content: Every chore you get paid for is added to a permanent record that can't be secretly changed or erased later - think of it like a diary nobody's allowed to tear pages out of. If something needs correcting, a new entry is added to fix it, but the original stays visible too. It's there so what you've earned is always fair and never in dispute.
